This is a senior FED-lead review, not an implementation task — you find and report defects, you never fix them, and you never edit any file.

WORKTREES (already checked out, deps installed — do not re-clone, do not run `npm start`):
- HEAD (review this): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/37973080-8be5-46e1-9aab-e2abcb81ea17/scratchpad/pr81-head

CRITICAL GIT TRAP — READ THIS FIRST: the local `develop` branch ref in the HEAD worktree has moved on past this PR's actual base and includes several unrelated merged PRs. If you run `git diff develop` you will see files that are NOT part of PR #81 (e.g. vitest.config.ts, zimmDrawer/*, zimmTabs, zimmSearchInput, zimmPdpDrawer, theme/foundation/sizes.ts, theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts, theme/components/zimmDrawerShared.ts, types/vendor.d.ts). GATE NUMBERS ALREADY MEASURED (do not re-run tsc/lint/vitest/audit:tokens yourself — read the rule docs and source, don't execute the tools):
tsc clean both sides; lint zero new PR-introduced errors; audit:tokens zero new unacknowledged violations (I have the actual log content, quoted below if you need cross-reference).

YOUR ANGLE: Conventions, structure, and tier ownership. Read these rule files directly at these repo paths for full text (they're long, read them yourself rather than relying on paraphrase): `.claude/rules/conventions.md`, `.claude/rules/components.md`, `.claude/rules/typescript.md`, `.claude/rules/css.md`, `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md`, `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`. Other reviewers cover: correctness/AC-satisfaction (not your job), contract fidelity / imageSize gating / swatch-variant regression (not your job), focus-trap/security internals (not your job), token/styling literal-value spot-checks (not your job — though tier-ownership of styling files IS your job).

SPECIFIC THINGS TO CHECK, ALL WITH CONCRETE STARTING POINTS I'VE ALREADY GATHERED:

1. **ZimmButton's new `sx` prop — backward compatibility.** Diff at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/index.tsx`:
```
+ import { Button as ChakraButton, IconButton, type SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
  type ZimmButtonBaseProps = {
    ...
+   /** Chakra `sx` passthrough — for a caller-owned recipe part, not a one-off inline style. */
+   sx?: SystemStyleObject;
  };
  export const ZimmButton = (props: ZimmButtonProps) => {
-   const { label, type = 'button', disabled = false, inverse = false, onClick, style } = props;
+   const { label, type = 'button', disabled = false, inverse = false, onClick, style, sx } = props;
    if (props.variant === 'icon') {
      return (<IconButton ... style={style} + sx={sx} />);
    }
    return (<ChakraButton ... style={style} + sx={sx}>{label}</ChakraButton>);
  };
```
All existing callers of ZimmButton found via grep: `zimmTabs/index.tsx`, `zimmInputAction/index.tsx`, `zimmDrawer/index.tsx`, `zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx` (these four are PRE-EXISTING, not touched by this PR's own new components) plus this PR's own new `zimmMediaTile`, `zimmGalleryOverlay`, `zimmProductGallery`. Confirm: (a) none of the four pre-existing callers pass a conflicting `sx`, so this really is purely additive/opt-in; (b) whether Chakra's prop-merge order for `sx` vs the component's own `zimmButton.css.ts` recipe (`_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled` etc.) could let a caller's `sx` silently clobber a pseudo-state the recipe defines — check `zimmButton.css.ts` for what pseudo-states exist and whether `styles.galleryButton` (the sx object the new gallery components pass, defined in `zimmProductGallery.css.ts`) touches any of the same CSS properties.

2. **"One canonical styling surface per component type"** (overrideStyling.md's core rule) — `zimmProductGallery/index.tsx` passes `sx={styles.galleryButton}` to `<ZimmButton variant="primary" inverse ...>` (three call sites, ~lines 220, 253, 318), where `styles.galleryButton` comes from `zimmProductGallery.css.ts`'s own recipe (~line 157). Read both `zimmButton.css.ts`'s own recipe AND `zimmProductGallery.css.ts`'s `galleryButton` part in full. Does `galleryButton`'s sx override/duplicate anything `zimmButton.css.ts`'s own `variant="primary"`+`inverse` styling already sets (color, background, padding, border)? If so, does this fragment single-source-of-truth styling for what a primary/inverse ZimmButton looks like — now split across two files that could disagree? This is exactly the concern overrideStyling.md's "One canonical styling surface" section warns about for buttons specifically (it explicitly says "`zimmButton.css.ts` ... is the single source of truth for button styling").

3. **pageContainer/index.tsx + globalStyles.ts — blast radius and Tier 2 governance.** Full diffs:
```diff
--- a/overrides/app/components/pageContainer/index.tsx
+++ b/overrides/app/components/pageContainer/index.tsx
+  // 'auto' (not '100%') when unboxed — a fixed width stops a negative marginX from actually
+  // growing the box, only letting it shift position (SFCC-731 full-bleed bug fix).
+  const widthValue = boxed ? '100%' : 'auto';
   return (
-    <Box width="100%" maxWidth={maxWidthValue} marginX={boxed ? 'auto' : undefined} paddingX={paddingXValue} {...rest}>
+    <Box width={widthValue} maxWidth={maxWidthValue} marginX={boxed ? 'auto' : undefined} paddingX={paddingXValue} {...rest}>
```
```diff
--- a/overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts
+++ b/overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts
+// `width: '100%'` (SFCC-731, 2026-09-03) is load-bearing. `#app-main` is a flex item, and
+// per the Flexbox spec, `margin: auto` disables cross-axis stretch regardless of `max-width` —
+// without an explicit width, `#app-main` shrink-to-fits to its content's intrinsic size instead
+// of filling its container, collapsing anything (like ZimmProductGallery) that relies on
+// flex-grow for its width. ...
 const zimmAppMain: SystemStyleObject = {
+  width: '100%',
   maxWidth: 'var(--zimm-grid-max-width)',
```
`PageContainer` is a generic, app-wide layout primitive (not PDP-specific), and `globalStyles.ts` composes `theme.styles.global` — CSS that ships on EVERY page. Tasks: (a) grep the ENTIRE `overrides/app/` tree for every caller of `<PageContainer` and check whether any pass `boxed={false}` or omit `boxed` (making it falsy/`undefined`, which per the ternary now resolves to `width: 'auto'` instead of the previous unconditional `width: '100%'`) OUTSIDE the PDP/gallery context — assess realistic regression risk on those other pages/callers; (b) per `protectedFiles.md`'s "Theme Component Styles (Owner: UI Designer — notify before changing)" section AND `frozenFiles.md`'s explicit note that `globalStyles.ts` "emits CSS on every page and therefore needs a named owner" — this is a Tier 2 file. Flag as a governance question: does anything in the PR's commits/description indicate UI-designer notification/review for this specific change? (c) Assess against AGENTS.md's "Minimal changes" rule and Hard Rule #10 ("never touch more than one protection tier... without confirming scope") — is a global `#app-main`/`PageContainer` behavior change appropriately scoped for a PDP-only ticket, or does it deserve to have been flagged/split out separately?

4. **JSDoc / stories / tests coverage** per components.md: check `zimmMediaTile/index.tsx` (reused by both zimmProductGallery AND zimmGalleryOverlay — qualifies as a "component used by ≥2 callers", so JSDoc is required), `zimmProductGallery/index.tsx`, `zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx`, `getDesktopLayoutCounts.ts`, `mapImageGroupsToGalleryMedia.ts`, `buildDisImageSrc.ts` all have adequate JSDoc. Confirm all three new components (`zimmMediaTile`, `zimmProductGallery`, `zimmGalleryOverlay`) have `*.stories.tsx` with a `Default` export plus meaningful named states (not just one flat story) and appropriate `*.test.ts(x)`. Check Storybook `title` categorisation — per components.md's table these are commerce/PDP-specific, so should be `Commerce/` or similar, not `Elements/`.

5. **Container/presentational separation** — grep the three new leaf components for any commerce SDK data-fetching hook call (`useCurrentBasket`, `useProduct`, etc. — `useIntl`/`useUiCopy` are fine, excepted). Expect clean, but confirm.

6. **CodeRabbit nitpick — MediaTile photo/video "duplication."** CodeRabbit flagged `zimmMediaTile/index.tsx` ~lines 71-103 as duplicating an "identical AspectRatio+fallback+Image block" between photo/video branches. I read the actual file and my own reading is: the `image` JSX variable (the AspectRatio-wrapped fallback/DynamicImage/Image logic) is computed ONCE (lines ~89-120) and referenced by both branches — it is NOT duplicated. What IS repeated is a much smaller one-line wrapper: `<AspectRatio ratio={GALLERY_ITEM_ASPECT_RATIO}>{image}</AspectRatio>` appears once in the photo branch's early return (~line 123) and again in the video branch's return (~line 128). Please read the actual current file yourself and confirm or refute my reading — is CodeRabbit's characterization ("identical AspectRatio+fallback+Image block") accurate, overstated, or understated? Assess real maintenance risk either way.

REPORT FORMAT: for every finding — `file:line`, one-sentence defect statement, concrete failure scenario, confidence (CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE), severity (🔴/🟡/🔵), UNIFORM or ONE-OFF. End with "What I tried to falsify" and "What I could not verify" sections. Don't pad — clean areas get one line.

=== buildDisImageSrc.ts ===
     1	/**
     2	 * SFCC-731 AC 19 — wraps a raw SFCC product-image URL into the templated "dynamic src" format
     3	 * base SFCC's `getResponsivePictureAttributes`/`DynamicImage` expect (see
     4	 * `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/responsive-image.js`'s own `getSrc` doc comment):
     5	 * a `[...]` segment containing a `{width}` placeholder that gets swapped in per breakpoint via
     6	 * SFCC's Dynamic Imaging Service query params (`sw` = scale width, `q` = quality).
     7	 *
     8	 * Deliberately does not build the `<picture>`/`srcSet` logic itself — that already exists in
     9	 * `DynamicImage` and shouldn't be duplicated. This is only the one SFCC-specific piece missing
    10	 * from that generic utility: the actual DIS query string for a given image URL.
    11	 *
    12	 * `data:`/`blob:` URLs are returned unchanged, with no template wrapper — DIS server-side
    13	 * resizing is meaningless for a URL that already *is* the image bytes (there's no server to ask),
    14	 * and appending a query-string-shaped suffix to a base64 payload corrupts it outright (the
    15	 * browser fails to decode it, `net::ERR_INVALID_URL`) rather than merely doing nothing useful.
    16	 *
    17	 * @param url - Raw SFCC image URL (`disBaseLink` or `link`), with or without existing query params.
    18	 * @param quality - DIS `q` param (0-100). Defaults to 80 — user-confirmed as the right baseline
    19	 *   for this brand's product photography (2026-09-05); 60, the base SFCC image-gallery
    20	 *   component's own default, showed visible compression artifacts on fabric/detail shots.
    21	 * @returns A templated src ready for `DynamicImage`'s `src` prop or base's `getSrc` helper.
    22	 */
    23	export const buildDisImageSrc = (url: string, quality = 80): string => {
    24	  if (url.startsWith('data:') || url.startsWith('blob:')) return url;
    25	  const separator = url.includes('?') ? '&' : '?';
    26	  return `${url}[${separator}sw={width}&q=${quality}]`;
    27	};
    28	
    29	/**
    30	 * Resolves a `buildDisImageSrc` template to a single concrete URL at a given width — the
    31	 * counterpart read side of the same `[...]`/`{width}` format, for a caller (e.g. a fixed-size
    32	 * thumbnail) that needs one resolved src rather than `DynamicImage`'s full responsive
    33	 * `<picture>`/`srcSet` treatment. A project-owned equivalent of base SFCC's own
    34	 * `getSrc` (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/responsive-image`), kept in-house so this
    35	 * templated-src format has one owner instead of a cross-package import for two lines of regex
    36	 * (CodeRabbit, PR #81).
    37	 *
    38	 * @param templatedSrc - Output of `buildDisImageSrc`, e.g. `https://x/img.jpg[?sw={width}&q=80]`.
    39	 * @param width - Concrete pixel width to substitute for `{width}`.
    40	 */
    41	export const resolveDisImageSrc = (templatedSrc: string, width: number): string =>
    42	  templatedSrc.replace(/\[([^\]]+)\]/g, '$1').replace(/\{[^}]+\}/g, String(width));

## PR #81 Review — Conventions, Structure & Tier Ownership

### 1–2. ZimmButton `sx` passthrough — backward compatibility + "one canonical styling surface"

**Backward compatibility: clean.** All four pre-existing callers (`zimmTabs/index.tsx:151-164`, `zimmInputAction/index.tsx:70-76`, `zimmDrawer/index.tsx:106`, `zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx:98-99`) pass no `sx`, and `sx` defaults to `undefined` through the new prop — purely additive. CONFIRMED clean.

**Finding A** — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductGallery/zimmProductGallery.css.ts:157-169` (`galleryButton`, consumed via `sx={styles.galleryButton}` at `zimmProductGallery/index.tsx:220,253,318`). The gallery's "Gallery +N" button is the **first production consumer of ZimmButton's `size="lg"` (default) styling anywhere in the app** — every pre-existing caller uses `variant="icon"` or `size="medium"`. Rather than exercising `zimmButton.css.ts`'s own `sizes.lg` (line 217-222: `h: BTN_HEIGHT_LG` = `'50px'`, plus a `textStyle: 'button'` the file's own TODO (lines 213-215) admits "isn't actually reaching the rendered button"), `galleryButton` fully substitutes height/padding/typography via `sx`, which Chakra applies with higher precedence than the recipe's `__css`. It uses `height: 'var(--zimm-size-action-height-lg)'` — `actionSizes.height.lg` in `foundation/sizes.ts:22` = **`'52px'`**, 2px different from `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`'s `'50px'`. Two typography properties (`lineHeight: lineHeights['3xs']`, `letterSpacing: letterSpacings.sm`) are raw JS-imported values rather than the `var(--zimm-font-lineheight-3xs)`/`var(--zimm-font-letterspacing-sm)` equivalents that **already exist** in `zimmTokens.ts:124,128` — inconsistent with the other 3 of 6 typography properties in the same object, which correctly use `var(--zimm-*)`. This is exactly the fragmentation overrideStyling.md's "One canonical styling surface per component type" section names buttons as the reference case for avoiding: any future second `size="lg"` primary button elsewhere in the app renders 2px shorter and hits the still-broken `textStyle` bug fresh, since this PR routed around the shared recipe instead of fixing or exercising it. CONFIRMED. 🟡. ONE-OFF (one component), but the underlying shared-recipe bug it papers over is not.

**Finding B** — `zimmProductGallery.css.ts:173-178` (`galleryDot`, via `sx={styles.galleryDot}` at `index.tsx:301`) and `zimmGalleryOverlay/zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts:120-133` (`closeButton`, via `sx={styles.closeButton}` at `zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx:190-196`) both pass `sx` to a `variant="icon"` ZimmButton and both override `_focusVisible` — `closeButton` also overrides `color`. Unlike Finding A, `variant="icon"` **does** have a live canonical example elsewhere (`zimmDrawer/index.tsx:106`'s close button, no `sx`, gets the plain `var(--zimm-focus-ring)` outline from `zimmButton.css.ts:168-172`). Two conceptually-identical "close an overlay" icon buttons (`zimmDrawer`'s vs `zimmGalleryOverlay`'s) will render **visibly different focus-ring treatments** (outline-ring vs. inset-box-shadow) purely because one goes through an `sx` override and the other doesn't. The `_focusVisible` override object itself (`outline: 'none'` / `boxShadow: 'inset 0 0 0 var(--zimm-border-width-default) var(--zimm-color-border-focus)'`) is byte-identical between `galleryDot` and `closeButton` — copy-pasted across two recipe files with no shared constant, a DRY violation on top of the styling-surface one. Each instance is individually commented (edge-clipping rationale), so this reads as deliberate, not careless — but it establishes a repeated pattern of the new `sx` escape hatch being used to partially re-own pseudo-states the recipe is supposed to solely own. CONFIRMED. 🟡. UNIFORM (recurs twice, same value, same mechanism).

*(Caveat: the `sx`-overrides-`__css` precedence claim rests on Chakra's documented style-prop precedence, not an executed runtime check — see "could not verify.")*

### 3. `pageContainer`/`globalStyles.ts` — blast radius and Tier 2 governance

**(a) Regression risk on other callers:** `PageContainer` currently has **zero other callers** anywhere in the repo — `grep -rn "PageContainer"` shows only this PR's own two usages in `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:951,1157`. So today there is no active regression; the `boxed={false} → width:'auto'` behavior change (`pageContainer/index.tsx:28,32`, replacing the previous unconditional `width:'100%'`) is exercised only by this PR's own code. The risk is latent, not active: `PageContainer` is a generically-named, unscoped `overrides/app/components/` primitive (not under `pages/product-detail/`), so any future page adopting it with `boxed={false}`/omitted inherits this changed default with no test coverage protecting non-PDP usage. PLAUSIBLE (future), not CONFIRMED (present). 🔵.

**(b) Tier 2 governance — confirmed gap, not just unverifiable.** `frozenFiles.md` states `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts` "is also Tier 2," and `protectedFiles.md`'s "Theme Component Styles (Owner: UI Designer — notify before changing)" section explicitly lists it. Checked all three enforcement layers directly:
- **CODEOWNERS** (full file read): the Tier 2 design-system block only has `overrides/app/theme/components/` (line 117) and Tier 1 only has `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`/`theme/index.ts` (lines 29-30). No line matches `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts` anywhere in the file, and there is no catch-all pattern. **No code-owner review is auto-requested for it at all.**
- **`.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml:219`**, the Tier 2 glob is `'overrides/app/theme/components/**'` — this cannot match the sibling file `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts`. Confirmed live on this PR: the bot's own "🟡 Tier 2 Protected Files Detected" comment (posted 2026-09-02) lists only `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` under "Files affected" — `globalStyles.ts` is absent despite being modified in the same PR.
- **PR evidence**: no commit message, PR body, or PR review/comment (`gh pr view 81`) mentions UI-designer notification for the `globalStyles.ts` change specifically. The only reviews are CodeRabbit and the author's own empty-body "COMMENTED" entries — no second-developer or designer approval is visible.

This is a real, standing gap in the tooling (not specific to this PR), but this PR is a live instance of exactly the failure mode it enables: a genuinely sitewide-blast-radius Tier 2 change shipped with none of its three documented safety nets firing. CONFIRMED. 🔴 (process-conformance/governance, not a code-correctness defect — the `width:'100%'` fix itself, per its own inline comment at `globalStyles.ts:228-233`, reads as a legitimate, well-reasoned CSS fix).

**(c) Minimal-changes / Hard Rule #10:** Only **one** protection tier is actually touched — "Theme Component Styles" (`theme/components/index.ts` + `globalStyles.ts`, both under the same protectedFiles.md section). No Tier 1 file is touched (confirmed against `frozenFiles.md`'s literal path list). So Hard Rule #10 ("never touch more than one protection tier... without confirming scope") is **not** technically triggered — I want to be precise here rather than over-claim. The narrower, real question is whether a global `#app-main` change belongs in a PDP-ticketed PR at all; given `PageContainer` has no other callers yet, the practical scope is currently self-contained, but the mechanism (a sitewide theme file) is a broader lever than the ticket needed, and per (b) above it went out without the review that same section explicitly calls for.

### 4. JSDoc / stories / tests coverage

- **JSDoc**: present and thorough on all three components (`zimmMediaTile/index.tsx:58-68`, `zimmProductGallery/index.tsx:76-85`, `zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx:67-81`) and all three utils (`getDesktopLayoutCounts.ts:8-19`, `mapImageGroupsToGalleryMedia.ts:4-12`, `buildDisImageSrc.ts:1-22` with full `@param`/`@returns`). Clean.
- **Tests**: `.test.ts(x)` exists for every new file (`zimmMediaTile/index.test.tsx`, `zimmProductGallery/index.test.tsx` + `getDesktopLayoutCounts.test.ts`, `zimmGalleryOverlay/index.test.tsx`, `mapImageGroupsToGalleryMedia.test.ts`, `buildDisImageSrc.test.ts`). Clean.
- **Missing `Default` story export** — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmMediaTile/index.stories.tsx`: exports are `Photo`, `EagerPhoto`, `Video`, `LoadFailure`, `ResponsiveWidths` (lines 31-63) — no export literally named `Default`, violating components.md's "Every story file has a `Default` named export." (`zimmProductGallery/index.stories.tsx:48` and `zimmGalleryOverlay/index.stories.tsx:71` both correctly have one.) CONFIRMED. 🔵. ONE-OFF.
- **Storybook categorisation** — `zimmMediaTile/index.stories.tsx:22`: `title: 'Elements/ZimmMediaTile'`. Its own JSDoc (line 65) describes it as reused specifically by the PDP's gallery/overlay states, and it depends on `buildDisImageSrc` (an SFCC-DIS-specific util) — this is commerce/PDP-specific per components.md's own test ("what does this component know about?"), and its two organism siblings both correctly use `Commerce/`. CONFIRMED miscategorization, inconsistent with siblings. 🔵. ONE-OFF.

### 5. Container/presentational separation

Clean. `grep` for `useCurrentBasket|useCurrentCustomer|useProduct|useQuery|useMutation|commerce-sdk-react` across all three new leaf components returns nothing. Only `useIntl` (all three) and `useUiCopy` (`zimmGalleryOverlay` only) appear — both explicitly excepted context-backed hooks per components.md. CONFIRMED clean.

### 6. CodeRabbit "MediaTile duplication" nitpick — stale, already resolved

Read the current file (`zimmMediaTile/index.tsx:89-128`) directly: your reading is correct. The `image` JSX (fallback / `DynamicImage` / plain `Image`, lines 89-120) is computed **once** and referenced by both branches; only the one-line `<AspectRatio ratio={GALLERY_ITEM_ASPECT_RATIO}>{image}</AspectRatio>` wrapper repeats (line 123 photo branch, line 128 video branch). Traced the history: CodeRabbit's nitpick (quoting a duplicated `AspectRatio`+fallback+`Image` block, no `DynamicImage`/`widths` branch at all) was reviewing commit `8e0e50c` (2026-09-05T01:58:42Z, the commit that first extracted `ZimmMediaTile`, with real duplication at that point). The very next content commit, `d7fb514e` (authored 2026-09-05 04:07:48 UTC, "AC9/AC19/AC25... DIS responsive images"), independently consolidated the exact block into the shared `const image =` as a side effect of adding the `widths`/`DynamicImage` branch — confirmed via `git show d7fb514e`, which shows the old duplicated form being replaced in that same commit. So CodeRabbit's characterization was accurate when written but is stale against current HEAD; it was not explicitly listed in `b10a54a`'s "address CodeRabbit findings" commit (likely already moot by then). CONFIRMED resolved. Remaining 2-line wrapper repetition carries negligible maintenance risk — it can't drift (same constant, same prop) the way the original fallback/`onError`/`DynamicImage` logic could have.

### Other observations (clean, one line each)

- `theme/components/index.ts` registration of `ZimmProductGallery`/`ZimmGalleryOverlay`/`ZimmMediaTile` is correctly done (import + `components` object entry for all three).
- `zimmColourSwatch`/`zimmColourSwatchGroup` (`ui-kits/atoms|molecules/`) and their co-located `.css.ts` files route correctly to Tier 3 (`ui-kits/`) / squad-only (`**/*.css.ts`) per CODEOWNERS' last-match-wins — not a tier-ownership gap, despite `protectedFiles.md`'s older kebab-case `swatch-group/` entry being a different, unrelated path.
- No Tier 1 file is touched anywhere in the 34-file diff (verified against `frozenFiles.md`'s literal path list).

**What I tried to falsify:**

- Checked whether `galleryButton`'s sx actually clobbers a color/hover/active/disabled pseudo-state (which would be a harder functional bug) — it does not; only sizing/typography, which I represented as the (still real) finding rather than overstating it as a visual-regression bug.
